records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה עַתָּ֣ה תִרְאֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֖ה לְפַרְעֹ֑ה כִּ֣י בְיָ֤ד חֲזָקָה֙ יְשַׁלְּחֵ֔ם וּבְיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה יְגָרְשֵׁ֖ם מֵאַרְצֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh; for by [a] strong hand he will let them go, and by [a] strong hand he will drive them out from his land.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses, "Now you are going to see what I will do to Pharaoh. Compelled by a strong hand, he will release them; compelled by a strong hand, he will drive them from his land."

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh; for by a strong hand he will let them go, and by a strong hand he will drive them out of his land."

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Now you will see what I am going to do to Pharaoh. A strong hand will force him to let the people go. A strong hand will even make him drive them out of his land."

decisions.choice: now you will see: God's answer to Moses' complaint in 5:22-23
decisions.reason: Moses said that God had not delivered his people at all (5:23). God answers that Moses is about to see what he will do.

decisions.choice: by a strong hand: under the pressure of God's power
alternatives: Pharaoh's own strong hand: he will forcefully expel them
decisions.reason: The hand is most likely God's power forcing Pharaoh, as in 3:19-20 and 13:9. It could also be Pharaoh's own hand: in the end he will not only let Israel go but push them out by force (12:31-33, 39). The phrase is said twice, and the second verb, "drive out", is the one used in 11:1 and 12:39.

decisions.choice: compelled by
decisions.reason: Balanced says how the hand works on Pharaoh without deciding whose hand it is.

records.heading: God promises to bring Israel out

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And spoke God to Moses and said to him, I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: God spoke to Moses and told him, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: And God spoke to Moses and said to him, "I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: God spoke to Moses again. He said, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh: God names himself as the one who speaks and acts
decisions.reason: The words open God's speech here and close it (verse 8), and they stand in the middle (verse 6). They introduce the commandments (20:2) and many laws (Leviticus 18:2-5). God's name is the guarantee of what he promises.

decisions.choice: God spoke: a new speech that goes back over the call of chapter 3
decisions.reason: After Moses' complaint, God repeats and extends what he said at the bush (3:6-17): his name, his covenant with the fathers, and his plan to bring Israel out.

decisions.choice: again
decisions.reason: Readable says that God has spoken to Moses before (3:4-4:17).

records.source: וָאֵרָ֗א אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֶל־יִצְחָ֥ק וְאֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּאֵ֣ל שַׁדָּ֑י וּשְׁמִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖עְתִּי לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob as God Almighty, and [by] my name Yahweh I did not make myself known to them.
pieces: I showed myself to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty, but I did not make myself known to them by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.3: And I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty, but [by] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I did not make myself known to them.

R.3: I came to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty. But I did not show them all that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, means.

decisions.choice: I did not make myself known by my name Yahweh: the fathers did not know the name in its full meaning, which God now shows by rescuing Israel
alternatives: Did I not make myself known to them by my name Yahweh?
the name itself was not revealed to them
decisions.reason: Genesis uses the name Yahweh many times, in the story and in the words of the fathers (Genesis 4:26; 12:8; 15:7; 28:13). So the sense is probably not that the name was unheard of before Moses. To "know" God in Exodus is to learn who he is by what he does: "you will know that I am Yahweh" when he brings Israel out (verse 7; 7:5). The fathers received the promises; their descendants will see them kept. Another reading takes the clause as a question, which Hebrew can mark without a question word: "by my name Yahweh did I not make myself known to them?" A third reading is that the name itself was first revealed to Moses.

decisions.choice: God Almighty: the title by which God gave his promises to the fathers
decisions.reason: God used this title when he made and renewed his promises (Genesis 17:1; 28:3; 35:11; 48:3). The meaning of the second word is not certain. It has been linked with words for "mountain" and for "to overpower". "Almighty" goes back to ancient Greek and Latin translations. It is a title, not God's personal name.

decisions.choice: as God Almighty: in the character of God Almighty
decisions.reason: The preposition means "as" or "in the role of": God made himself known to the fathers under this title.

decisions.choice: all that my name means
decisions.reason: Readable says what "did not make myself known by my name" most likely means here, following the first meaning decision. The other readings are in the footnote.

records.source: וְגַ֨ם הֲקִמֹ֤תִי אֶת־בְּרִיתִי֙ אִתָּ֔ם לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן אֵ֛ת אֶ֥רֶץ מְגֻרֵיהֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־גָּ֥רוּ בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And also I established my covenant with them to give to them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, in which they sojourned.
pieces: I also confirmed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with them, that I would give them the land of Canaan, the land where they stayed as foreigners.

L.4: And I also established {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, in which they sojourned.

R.4: I also made a covenant with them. I promised to give them the land of Canaan. They lived there, but it was not yet their own land.

decisions.choice: established: set up, confirmed
decisions.reason: The verb means to make a covenant stand. It is used in God's covenant with Abraham (Genesis 17:7, 19).

decisions.choice: the land of their sojournings: the land where they lived as resident foreigners
decisions.reason: A sojourner lived among a people without owning land or having full rights there. Abraham calls himself one in Canaan and has to buy a field to bury Sarah (Genesis 23:4). The words repeat God's promise in Genesis 17:8: "the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan".

decisions.choice: they lived there, but it was not yet their own land
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a sojourner was.

records.source: וְגַ֣ם׀אֲנִ֣י שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶֽת־נַאֲקַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִצְרַ֖יִם מַעֲבִדִ֣ים אֹתָ֑ם וָאֶזְכֹּ֖ר אֶת־בְּרִיתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And also I have heard the groaning of [the] sons of Israel whom Egypt is making work, and I have remembered my covenant.
pieces: I myself have now heard the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} groaning under the slavery the Egyptians force on them, and I have kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant in mind.

L.5: And I also have heard the groaning of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, whom Egypt is making work [as slaves], and I have remembered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant.

R.5: I have heard the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} groaning because the Egyptians force them to work as slaves. I have remembered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, and I will keep it.

decisions.choice: the groaning ... I have remembered my covenant: the words of 2:24
decisions.reason: In 2:24 God heard Israel's groaning and remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Here God says it himself.

decisions.choice: remembered: called to mind in order to act
decisions.reason: When God "remembers" he acts on what he remembers (Genesis 8:1; 30:22). It does not mean he had forgotten.

decisions.choice: I: stressed
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis: it is God himself who has heard.

decisions.choice: and I will keep it
decisions.reason: Readable says what "remember" means here, following the second meaning decision.

decisions.choice: slavery; work as slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level where it appears, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֥ר לִבְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֘לאֲנִ֣י יְהוָה֒ וְהוֹצֵאתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֗ם מִתַּ֨חַת֙ סִבְלֹ֣ת מִצְרַ֔יִם וְהִצַּלְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵעֲבֹדָתָ֑ם וְגָאַלְתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֔ה וּבִשְׁפָטִ֖ים גְּדֹלִֽים׃
records.gloss: Therefore say to [the] sons of Israel, I [am] Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under [the] burdens of Egypt, and I will deliver you from their slavery, and I will redeem you with [an] arm outstretched and with judgments great.
pieces: So tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will lead you out from under the forced labor of the Egyptians and rescue you from serving them as slaves. I will redeem you with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arm stretched out and with great acts of judgment.

L.6: Therefore say to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, 'I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of Egypt, and I will deliver you from their slavery, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great judgments.

R.6: So tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will lead you out from under the hard work the Egyptians force on you. I will rescue you so that you are no longer their slaves. I will redeem you, as a close relative pays to set a family member free. I will reach out with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great power and punish Egypt with terrible judgments.

decisions.choice: redeem: act as the close relative who frees a family member
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the nearest relative, who had the duty to buy back family land or to free a relative sold into slavery (Leviticus 25:25, 47-49; Ruth 4:4-6). God acts for Israel as its next of kin; he has called Israel his firstborn son (4:22).

decisions.choice: an outstretched arm: power put into action
decisions.reason: The arm is a picture of strength; stretched out, it is at work. The phrase is often used of the exodus (Deuteronomy 4:34; 5:15; Psalm 136:12).

decisions.choice: great judgments: acts of judgment on Egypt
decisions.reason: The word means sentences carried out, punishments. The plagues are God's judgments on Egypt and its gods (7:4; 12:12).

decisions.choice: I will ...: a chain of promises framed by "I am Yahweh"
decisions.reason: Verses 6-8 join seven promises with "and": bring out, deliver, redeem, take as a people, be your God, bring in, give the land. "I am Yahweh" stands before them (verse 6) and after them (verse 8).

decisions.choice: burdens: forced labor
decisions.reason: The word is the one used of Israel's forced labor in 1:11; 2:11; 5:4.

decisions.choice: as a close relative pays to set a family member free; my great power; punish Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable explains "redeem" and "outstretched arm", and says that the judgments fall on Egypt (12:12).

decisions.choice: serving them as slaves; their slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level where it appears, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

records.source: וְלָקַחְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֥ם לִי֙ לְעָ֔ם וְהָיִ֥יתִי לָכֶ֖ם לֵֽאלֹהִ֑ים וִֽידַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם הַמּוֹצִ֣יא אֶתְכֶ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת סִבְל֥וֹת מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And I will take you to me for [a] people, and I will be to you for God, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh your God, the [one] bringing you out from under [the] burdens of Egypt.
pieces: I will claim you as a people for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will be your God. And you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, the one who brings you out from under the forced labor of Egypt.

L.7: And I will take you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as a people, and I will be God to you; and you shall know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt.

R.7: I will make you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You will know that I am the one who leads you out from under the hard work in Egypt.

decisions.choice: I will take you as my people and be your God: the words of the covenant
decisions.reason: These words state the bond between God and Israel, promised to Abraham (Genesis 17:7-8) and repeated in the law and the prophets (Leviticus 26:12; Jeremiah 31:33).

decisions.choice: you will know: you will learn by what you see me do
decisions.reason: The knowledge comes from experience. It answers verse 3 and Pharaoh's "I do not know Yahweh" (5:2).

decisions.choice: who brings you out: a participle that names God by what he does
decisions.reason: The form does not fix a time. When Israel comes to know God, he will be the one who brought them out (20:2).

records.source: וְהֵבֵאתִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֨אתִי֙ אֶת־יָדִ֔י לָתֵ֣ת אֹתָ֔הּ לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹ֑ב וְנָתַתִּ֨י אֹתָ֥הּ לָכֶ֛ם מוֹרָשָׁ֖ה אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will bring you into the land which I lifted up my hand to give it to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, and I will give it to you [as a] possession; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: I will bring you into the land that I promised with an oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and I will give it to you to hold as your own. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

L.8: And I will bring you into the land which I lifted up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it to you [as] a possession. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

R.8: I will bring you into the land I promised with an oath to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you, and it will belong to you. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

decisions.choice: I lifted up my hand: I swore
decisions.reason: A raised hand went with an oath (Genesis 14:22). The phrase is used of God's oath about the land (Numbers 14:30; Ezekiel 20:5-6). The oath to Abraham is in Genesis 22:16-17 and 26:3.

decisions.choice: a possession: land held as one's own and passed on
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb used of taking over land as an inheritance (Genesis 15:7).

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh: the speech ends as it began
decisions.reason: The words of verses 2 and 6 close the promises.

decisions.choice: promised with an oath
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the raised hand means. Literal keeps the picture.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר מֹשֶׁ֛ה כֵּ֖ן אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֤א שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה מִקֹּ֣צֶר ר֔וּחַ וּמֵעֲבֹדָ֖ה קָשָֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: And spoke Moses thus to [the] sons of Israel, and not they listened to Moses from shortness of spirit and from labor hard.
pieces: Moses passed this on to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, but they would not listen to him. Their spirits were worn down and their slavery was cruel.

L.9: And Moses spoke thus to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, but they did not listen to Moses, because of shortness of spirit and because of hard labor.

R.9: Moses told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} what God had said. But they would not listen to him. They had lost all hope, and their hard work as slaves had worn them out.

decisions.choice: shortness of spirit: discouragement; spirits too worn down to hope
decisions.reason: To be "short" in spirit or soul is to be unable to bear any more (Numbers 21:4; Job 21:4). The word for spirit also means breath, so the picture may be of people gasping under their burden.

decisions.choice: hard labor: the words of 1:14
decisions.reason: Their work was made bitter "with hard labor" in 1:14. In 4:31 the people believed Moses; now, after 5:6-21, they cannot listen.

decisions.choice: what God had said
decisions.reason: Readable says what "thus" refers to.

decisions.choice: slavery; work as slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level where it appears, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

records.heading: Moses sent again to Pharaoh

records.source: בֹּ֣א דַבֵּ֔ר אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וִֽישַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאַרְצֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Go in, speak to Pharaoh, [the] king of Egypt, and he will let go [the] sons of Israel from his land.
pieces: "Go in to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and tell him to release the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} from his country."

L.11: "Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he may let the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel go from his land."

R.11: "Go to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Tell him he must let the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} leave his land."

decisions.choice: and he will let go: so that he lets them go
alternatives: and he will let them go (a promise)
decisions.reason: The form after a command can state its purpose ("speak, so that he lets go") or the message itself ("tell him to let go"). Either way, Moses is sent to demand Israel's release.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֔ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵ֤ן בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֹֽא־שָׁמְע֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְאֵיךְ֙ יִשְׁמָעֵ֣נִי פַרְעֹ֔ה וַאֲנִ֖י עֲרַ֥ל שְׂפָתָֽיִם׃פ
records.gloss: And spoke Moses before Yahweh, saying, look, [the] sons of Israel have not listened to me, and how will listen to me Pharaoh, and I [am] uncircumcised of lips?
pieces: But Moses answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Even the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have not listened to me. How can I expect Pharaoh to listen, when I speak so poorly?"

L.12: And Moses spoke before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Look, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel have not listened to me; how then will Pharaoh listen to me, when I [am] uncircumcised of lips?"

R.12: But Moses said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} would not listen to me. So how will Pharaoh listen to me? I am not good at speaking."

decisions.choice: uncircumcised of lips: unskilled in speech
decisions.reason: "Uncircumcised" is used of something closed or unfit for its task: ears that do not hear (Jeremiah 6:10), a heart that does not obey (Leviticus 26:41). Moses means that his lips cannot speak well, as he said in 4:10.

decisions.choice: look ... how: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If Israel, who would gain by the message, did not listen, Pharaoh, who would lose by it, will listen even less.

decisions.choice: I speak so poorly; I am not good at speaking
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means. Literal keeps "uncircumcised of lips".

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹן֒ וַיְצַוֵּם֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ס
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron, and he commanded them to [the] sons of Israel and to Pharaoh, [the] king of Egypt, to bring out [the] sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and Aaron and gave them a charge for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and for Pharaoh, king of Egypt: they were to bring the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of the land of Egypt.

L.13: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded them concerning the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and concerning Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel out of the land of Egypt.

R.13: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and Aaron. He gave them orders to take to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. He commanded them to lead the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: commanded them to the sons of Israel and to Pharaoh: gave them a charge for both
alternatives: commanded them concerning the sons of Israel and Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "to" or "concerning". God sends Moses and Aaron with a charge to Israel and a demand to Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: a summary before the family list
decisions.reason: The verse sums up the charge to Moses and Aaron. The list of verses 14-25 follows, and verses 26-27 return to the same words, so that the list shows who these two men are.

records.source: אֵ֖לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֣י בֵית־אֲבֹתָ֑ם בְּנֵ֨י רְאוּבֵ֜ן בְּכֹ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל חֲנ֤וֹךְ וּפַלּוּא֙ חֶצְר֣וֹן וְכַרְמִ֔י אֵ֖לֶּה מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת רְאוּבֵֽן׃
records.gloss: These [are the] heads of [the] house of their fathers; [the] sons of Reuben, [the] firstborn of Israel: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi; these [are the] clans of Reuben.
pieces: Here are the heads of the family lines. Reuben was Israel's firstborn; his sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. These were the Reubenite clans.

L.14: These [are] the heads of their fathers' houses: the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi; these [are] the clans of Reuben.

R.14: These were the leaders of the family groups. Reuben was the oldest son of Jacob, who was also called Israel. Reuben's sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. Their families became the clans of Reuben.

decisions.choice: fathers' houses ... clans: the units of a tribe
decisions.reason: A "father's house" was an extended family under its head. Several such families made up a clan, and clans made up a tribe (Joshua 7:14).

decisions.choice: the sons of Reuben: the list of Genesis 46:8-11
decisions.reason: The names follow Genesis 46:9 and Numbers 26:5-6. The list gives Reuben and Simeon briefly and stops at Levi, because its aim is to show the family of Moses and Aaron.

decisions.choice: Israel: Jacob, the man
decisions.reason: Here Israel is Jacob himself, renamed in Genesis 32:28, not the people.

decisions.choice: Jacob, who was also called Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says who Israel is here.

records.heading: The family lines of Moses and Aaron

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֗וֹן יְמוּאֵ֨ל וְיָמִ֤ין וְאֹ֨הַד֙ וְיָכִ֣ין וְצֹ֔חַר וְשָׁא֖וּל בֶּן־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑ית אֵ֖לֶּה מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת שִׁמְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jakin and Zohar and Shaul, [the] son of the Canaanite [woman]; these [are the] clans of Simeon.
pieces: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar, and Shaul, whose mother was a Canaanite. These were the Simeonite clans.

L.15: And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jakin and Zohar, and Shaul the son of the Canaanite [woman]; these [are] the clans of Simeon.

R.15: Simeon's sons were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar, and Shaul. Shaul's mother was a woman from Canaan. These were the clans of Simeon.

decisions.choice: the son of the Canaanite woman: Shaul's mother was a Canaanite
decisions.reason: The same note is in Genesis 46:10. The fathers warned against marrying Canaanites (Genesis 24:3; 28:1), though Judah also married one (Genesis 38:2).

decisions.choice: Jemuel ... Ohad: names that differ in other lists
decisions.reason: Numbers 26:12 and 1 Chronicles 4:24 give the first son as Nemuel and leave out Ohad. This verse agrees with Genesis 46:10.

records.source: וְאֵ֨לֶּה שְׁמ֤וֹת בְּנֵֽי־לֵוִי֙ לְתֹ֣לְדֹתָ֔ם גֵּרְשׁ֕וֹן וּקְהָ֖ת וּמְרָרִ֑י וּשְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י לֵוִ֔י שֶׁ֧בַע וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] names of [the] sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon and Kohath and Merari; and [the] years of [the] life of Levi [were] seven and thirty and [a] hundred year[s].
pieces: These are the names of Levi's sons, by their family lines: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.

L.16: And these [are] the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon and Kohath and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi [were] 137 years.

R.16: Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Each of them became the father of a family line. Levi lived to be 137 years old.

decisions.choice: according to their generations: by their family lines
decisions.reason: The word means descendants or family histories, as in "these are the generations of" in Genesis (Genesis 2:4; 25:19).

decisions.choice: the years of Levi's life: given only for the line leading to Moses
decisions.reason: The list gives the ages of Levi, Kohath (verse 18), and Amram (verse 20), Moses' direct ancestors, and of no one else.

decisions.choice: each of them became the father of a family line
decisions.reason: Readable says what "according to their generations" means.

records.source: בְּנֵ֥י גֵרְשׁ֛וֹן לִבְנִ֥י וְשִׁמְעִ֖י לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei according to their clans.
pieces: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei, each with his clan.

L.17: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to their clans.

R.17: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei. Each one became the head of a clan.

decisions.choice: according to their clans: each son heads a clan
decisions.reason: The clans of Libni and Shimei are named in Numbers 3:18-21.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י קְהָ֔ת עַמְרָ֣ם וְיִצְהָ֔ר וְחֶבְר֖וֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵ֑ל וּשְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י קְהָ֔ת שָׁלֹ֧שׁ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar and Hebron and Uzziel; and [the] years of [the] life of Kohath [were] three and thirty and [a] hundred year[s].
pieces: Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.

L.18: And the sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar and Hebron and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath [were] 133 years.

R.18: Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived to be 133 years old.

decisions.choice: Kohath ... Amram: a family line that may skip generations
alternatives: a complete list: Amram is Moses' father
decisions.reason: Kohath went down to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46:11), and Israel stayed in Egypt 430 years (12:40). Four generations from Levi to Moses fit that span only if the list names the main links and leaves some out, as other lists do (Matthew 1:8 compared with 1 Chronicles 3:11-12). Amram may then be an ancestor of Moses rather than his father, though verse 20 reads most naturally as father and son.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֥י מְרָרִ֖י מַחְלִ֣י וּמוּשִׁ֑י אֵ֛לֶּה מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הַלֵּוִ֖י לְתֹלְדֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; these [are the] clans of the Levite according to their generations.
pieces: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of Levi, listed by their family lines.

L.19: And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These [are] the clans of the Levites according to their generations.

R.19: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites, family by family.

decisions.choice: the Levite: the tribe of Levi as a whole
decisions.reason: The singular stands for the whole tribe. The three sons of Levi head the three branches that later serve at the tabernacle (Numbers 3:17-37).

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח עַמְרָ֜ם אֶת־יוֹכֶ֤בֶד דֹּֽדָתוֹ֙ ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד ל֔וֹ אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֖ן וְאֶת־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וּשְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י עַמְרָ֔ם שֶׁ֧בַע וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And took Amram Jochebed his father's sister for himself as [a] wife, and she bore to him Aaron and Moses; and [the] years of [the] life of Amram [were] seven and thirty and [a] hundred year[s].
pieces: Amram took as his wife Jochebed, the sister of his father, and she bore him Aaron and Moses. The length of Amram's life was 137 years.

L.20: And Amram took Jochebed his father's sister for himself as wife, and she bore him Aaron and Moses; and the years of the life of Amram [were] 137 years.

R.20: Amram married Jochebed, his father's sister. She was the mother of Aaron and Moses. Amram lived to be 137 years old.

decisions.choice: Jochebed, his father's sister: Amram married his aunt
decisions.reason: The law given later at Sinai forbids marrying one's father's sister (Leviticus 18:12; 20:19). The text reports the marriage plainly; it took place before that law. Jochebed is named again in Numbers 26:59, where she is called a daughter of Levi.

decisions.choice: his father's sister: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint reads "the daughter of his father's brother", making Jochebed Amram's cousin. The Hebrew text is followed. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: Aaron and Moses: Miriam is not named
alternatives: and Miriam their sister (Septuagint, Samaritan Pentateuch)
decisions.reason: The Septuagint and the Samaritan Pentateuch add "and Miriam their sister" (compare Numbers 26:59). The Hebrew text, which does not have the words, is followed. Reviewers should check the evidence.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י יִצְהָ֑ר קֹ֥רַח וָנֶ֖פֶג וְזִכְרִֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Izhar: Korah and Nepheg and Zikri.
pieces: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zikri.

L.21: And the sons of Izhar: Korah and Nepheg and Zikri.

R.21: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zikri.

decisions.choice: Korah: the cousin of Moses who later rebels
decisions.reason: Korah later leads a revolt against Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16:1-3). Since Izhar was Amram's brother (verse 18), Korah was their cousin.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י עֻזִּיאֵ֑ל מִֽישָׁאֵ֥ל וְאֶלְצָפָ֖ן וְסִתְרִֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Uzziel: Mishael and Elzaphan and Sithri.
pieces: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.

L.22: And the sons of Uzziel: Mishael and Elzaphan and Sithri.

R.22: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.

decisions.choice: Mishael and Elzaphan: the cousins who carry out Nadab and Abihu
decisions.reason: Moses calls on these two to carry away the bodies of Aaron's sons (Leviticus 10:4).

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־אֱלִישֶׁ֧בַע בַּת־עַמִּינָדָ֛ב אֲח֥וֹת נַחְשׁ֖וֹן ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד ל֗וֹ אֶת־נָדָב֙ וְאֶת־אֲבִיה֔וּא אֶת־אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְאֶת־אִֽיתָמָֽר׃
records.gloss: And took Aaron Elisheba, [the] daughter of Amminadab, [the] sister of Nahshon, for himself as [a] wife, and she bore to him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
pieces: Aaron married Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon, and she bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

L.23: And Aaron took Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, for himself as wife, and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

R.23: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon. Their sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

decisions.choice: Amminadab ... Nahshon: a leading family of Judah
decisions.reason: Nahshon was the leader of the tribe of Judah (Numbers 1:7; 2:3) and an ancestor of David (Ruth 4:20-22). Aaron's marriage joined the priestly family to this line.

decisions.choice: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, Ithamar: the first priests after Aaron
decisions.reason: Nadab and Abihu die for offering unauthorized fire (Leviticus 10:1-2). Eleazar and Ithamar carry on the priesthood (Numbers 3:4).

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י קֹ֔רַח אַסִּ֥יר וְאֶלְקָנָ֖ה וַאֲבִיאָסָ֑ף אֵ֖לֶּה מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הַקָּרְחִֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Korah: Assir and Elkanah and Abiasaph; these [are the] clans of the Korahite.
pieces: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. These were the Korahite clans.

L.24: And the sons of Korah: Assir and Elkanah and Abiasaph; these [are] the clans of the Korahites.

R.24: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. These were the clans that came from Korah.

decisions.choice: the sons of Korah: a line that survives
decisions.reason: When Korah died in his revolt, his sons did not die (Numbers 26:11). Several psalms are headed "of the sons of Korah" (Psalms 42; 44-49).

records.source: וְאֶלְעָזָ֨ר בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֜ן לָקַֽח־ל֨וֹ מִבְּנ֤וֹת פּֽוּטִיאֵל֙ ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד ל֖וֹ אֶת־פִּֽינְחָ֑ס אֵ֗לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֛י אֲב֥וֹת הַלְוִיִּ֖ם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And Eleazar, [the] son of Aaron, took for himself from [the] daughters of Putiel for himself as [a] wife, and she bore to him Phinehas; these [are the] heads of [the] fathers of the Levites according to their clans.
pieces: Eleazar son of Aaron married one of Putiel's daughters, and she bore him Phinehas. These were the heads of the Levite families, clan by clan.

L.25: And Eleazar the son of Aaron took for himself [one] of the daughters of Putiel as wife, and she bore him Phinehas. These [are] the heads of the fathers of the Levites according to their clans.

R.25: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of the daughters of Putiel. Their son was Phinehas. These were the leaders of the Levite families and their clans.

decisions.choice: Phinehas: the priest of Numbers 25
decisions.reason: Phinehas acts with zeal for God and is given a covenant of lasting priesthood (Numbers 25:7-13). The list ends with him, three generations after Amram.

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: the heads of the fathers' houses
decisions.reason: The phrase is a short form of "heads of fathers' houses" (verse 14), the family heads of the tribe.

records.source: ה֥וּא אַהֲרֹ֖ן וּמֹשֶׁ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם הוֹצִ֜יאוּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל־צִבְאֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: That [is the] Aaron and Moses to whom said Yahweh, bring out [the] sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt by their hosts.
pieces: This Aaron and this Moses are the ones {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told, "Lead the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of the land of Egypt, company by company."

L.26: That [is the] Aaron and Moses to whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Bring the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel out of the land of Egypt according to their hosts."

R.26: Aaron and Moses from this family are the men {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to. He told them, "Lead the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of Egypt in their groups, like an army."

decisions.choice: that is the Aaron and Moses: the very men named in the list
decisions.reason: The words point back to verse 20 and pick up the story from verse 13. Aaron is named first, as in the list, because he was the elder (7:7).

decisions.choice: by their hosts: in organized companies, like an army
decisions.reason: The word is used of armies. Israel leaves Egypt in ordered ranks, not as a fleeing crowd (7:4; 12:17, 41, 51).

decisions.choice: company by company; in their groups, like an army
decisions.reason: "Hosts" is old-fashioned. Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: from this family
decisions.reason: Readable says what "that Aaron and Moses" points back to.

records.source: הֵ֗ם הַֽמְדַבְּרִים֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם ה֥וּא מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃
records.gloss: They [are] the [ones] speaking to Pharaoh, [the] king of Egypt, to bring out [the] sons of Israel from Egypt; that [is] Moses and Aaron.
pieces: It was they who went before Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and spoke to him so that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} might be brought out of Egypt: this Moses and this Aaron.

L.27: They [are] the ones who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel out of Egypt; that [is] Moses and Aaron.

R.27: These two men, Moses and Aaron, were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. They told him to let the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} leave Egypt.

decisions.choice: they ... that is Moses and Aaron: the names repeated in reverse order
decisions.reason: Verse 26 names Aaron and Moses; verse 27 ends with Moses and Aaron. The repetition closes the family list and returns to the story with Moses in the lead.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּי֨וֹם דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃פ
records.gloss: And it was on [the] day [that] spoke Yahweh to Moses in [the] land of Egypt,
pieces: Now on the day when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,

L.28: And it was on the day [when] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,

R.28: This is what happened when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses in Egypt.

decisions.choice: and it was on the day: the story picks up again
decisions.reason: Verses 28-30 repeat verses 10-12 to return to the story after the family list. God's answer comes in 7:1.

decisions.choice: on the day: at the time
decisions.reason: The phrase means "when" and does not limit the event to one day.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹ֖ר אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה דַּבֵּ֗ר אֶל־פַּרְעֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י דֹּבֵ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: and spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying, I [am] Yahweh; speak to Pharaoh, [the] king of Egypt, all that I [am] speaking to you.
pieces: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Repeat to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, every word I speak to you."

L.29: and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying, "I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I [am] speaking to you."

R.29: He said, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Give Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, every message I give you."

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh. Speak to Pharaoh: verses 2 and 11 repeated
decisions.reason: The repetition takes the reader back to God's words before the family list.

decisions.choice: He
decisions.reason: Readable uses a pronoun, since verse 28 has just named the LORD.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הֵ֤ן אֲנִי֙ עֲרַ֣ל שְׂפָתַ֔יִם וְאֵ֕יךְ יִשְׁמַ֥ע אֵלַ֖י פַּרְעֹֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And said Moses before Yahweh, look, I [am] uncircumcised of lips, and how will listen to me Pharaoh?
pieces: But Moses replied in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "I am such a poor speaker. How will Pharaoh ever listen to me?"

L.30: And Moses said before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Look, I [am] uncircumcised of lips; how then will Pharaoh listen to me?"

R.30: But Moses said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "I am not good at speaking. Why would Pharaoh listen to me?"

decisions.choice: uncircumcised of lips: Moses' objection of verse 12 repeated
decisions.reason: On the picture, see verse 12. God answers it in 7:1-2: Aaron will speak for Moses.

decisions.choice: I am such a poor speaker; I am not good at speaking
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, Balanced and Readable say what the picture means. Literal keeps it.
